title: Deployment orchestration quickstart — compact onboarding & fallback policy visuals
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design a compact, keyboard-first quickstart flow and a set of product screenshots demonstrating progressive deployment orchestration: stepwise canary exposure, lightweight A/B split setup, and clear fallback policy UX. Focus on small-screen and PWA rendering, accessibility, and minimizing cognitive load for first-time users. Deliverables: annotated screenshot pack, Figma flows for embedded quickstart, copy for microcopy and tooltips, and exportable PNG/JPEG assets for docs and marketing.
acceptance_criteria: Crafted 6 annotated screens (desktop + mobile) covering: create deployment, set canary %, set A/B split, define fallback policy, review & confirm, success state with telemetry snapshot.
Figma file with components tokenized and responsive variants included.
Accessibility review completed with contrast ratios and keyboard flows documented.
Exported screenshot pack uploaded to Drive with naming convention and metadata.
Design walkthrough delivered to PM, Eng, and Docs; sign-off recorded in comments.

Export assets and upload to Drive + update Confluence PRD (Avery)
Handoff meeting with Eng + Docs; record feedback (Morgan)
design_notes: Primary goal: reduce setup time for first-time rollout users by exposing only the minimum fields and providing progressive disclosure for advanced options.
Compact layout: condensed form fields + inline validation to avoid modal wizards that block context.
Keyboard-first: ensure all interactive elements reachable by tab and provide clear focus styles; include shortcut hint ("k") to jump to quickstart from dashboard.
Fallback policy microcopy options: prefer 'Pause' + 'Route to stable' wording rather than 'Rollback' to avoid alarm; include last-successful-model snapshot info.
A/B split UI: use linear slider with percent chips for exact numeric input; show cost estimate delta and expected latency band next to each variant.
Telemetry snapshot: lightweight sparkline + P99 latency + error rate; link to full dashboard for deeper analysis.
Trade-offs: removed large traffic heatmap from quickstart to keep initial flow under 1 minute; advanced heatmap retained in the rollout details page.
Accessibility: use 4.5:1 contrast for primary CTA on all variants; provide aria-live region for success/failure messages.
Localization: leave room for long-form translations in labels (95th percentile width tested).
